title: This Is How We Do It
reasoning: crema and ffmpeg (two different-method detectors) fully agree on F minor; librosa's F major dissent is explained above as a parallel-quality template artifact from the Phrygian flat-II chord rather than independent disagreement. Two authoritative human sources corroborate independently: Musicnotes' published original key (F minor) and Hooktheory's multi-contributor TheoryTab (F Phrygian, same tonic and quality once collapsed). ffmpeg's r (0.721) alone sits in the gray zone, but the explained dissent plus two independent human sources clear the bar for HIGH. Mode is recorded as phrygian because Hooktheory names it explicitly; the Ableton tag stays collapsed to F minor per the collapse rule.
tonicCheck: The chord list alternates an F#/Gb major triad against Fm and F, which is exactly Hooktheory's stated Fm7->Gbmaj7 vamp -- the textbook Phrygian flat-II signature a half-step above the tonic. The 58-62s key-flicker shows Fm alternating with A#m (=Bbm, the iv of F minor), a sensible i-iv wobble rather than a competing center. Early flicker (Em/A/A#/B/G#m at r 0.31-0.64) is just an unstable intro. Nothing in the chord data supports F major or a relative-key alternative; the flat-II chord a half-step above the tonic is the likely cause of librosa's F major misread, since that kind of chromatic clash is a known confuser for KS-template correlation.

title: MILLION DOLLAR BABY
reasoning: librosa (0.706), CREMA, and ffmpeg keydetect (r=0.855, trust band) all agree on F# minor, and the three failed independently enough (CS-based librosa/ffmpeg vs. the differently-built CREMA) for that agreement to count as real corroboration rather than shared bias. CREMA's runner-up, B minor at 0.7713 separation, is the iv chord of F# minor (not the relative major, A), so this isn't the classic relative-key trap — it's the same close diatonic relation the chord loop itself uses. Hooktheory's multi-contributor TheoryTab independently confirms F# minor and explains the raw chord list's F#/F#m flicker as minor-7 voicings, not a real modal ambiguity. BPM is a clean match: 138 online vs. 137.74 rough, no octave discrepancy.
tonicCheck: All three detectors agree on F# minor and ffmpeg sits in the trust band (r=0.855). The raw chord list alternates F#/F#m, B/Bm, C#/C#m, which looks like a major/minor tonic conflict, but Hooktheory's chart shows the real progression is a i-iv-i loop of minor-7 chords (F#m7 - Bm7 - G#m7), several played as rootless voicings — the chord recognizer is reading the missing or ambiguous third/seventh as a major triad. No competing tonal center (A major, the relative) ever surfaces as a sustained chord. The flicker log's early instability (t<1s, r 0.65-0.79) is intro noise; it settles into a stable F#/F#m read by ~24s, consistent with a i-iv vamp rather than a genuine ambiguity.
